newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Marauding Zairean soldiers rob ferry passengers.
newsitem.headline: Marauding Zairean soldiers rob ferry passengers.

text.p: Zairean soldiers trying to escape eastern Zaire's battle zone with their families stormed aboard a Tanzanian ferry on Lake Tanganyika and stole luggage, money and a cargo of fish, Tanzanian officials said on Friday.

They said an undetermined number of soldiers forced their way on to the Tanzania Railways Corporation-owned ferry Mwongozo on Monday at the Zairean port of Kalundu on the western shore of Lake Tanganyika.

Accompanied by family members and large amounts of luggage and household goods, the soldiers demanded to be taken to the Zairean port of Kalemie outside the conflict zone between troops and Tutsi rebels.
At one point the ferry, loaded with more than 3,500 passengers, the soldiers, their families and baggage, listed dangerously, said a Tanzanian railways official who declined to be identified.
The soldiers then spotted a Zairean-owned ferry, the Zongwe, arriving in Kalundu bound for Kalemie and left the Mwongozo.
But they returned later with their weapons to recover their baggage and at the same time robbed passengers of their money and belongings and stole the Mwongozo's cargo of fish.
The officials said that after the incident the TRC suspended ship and ferry services between the Tanzanian port of Kigoma and Zairean ports on Lake Tanganyika because of rising insecurity.
The official, who received reports of the incident relayed from the Mwongozo's captain by radio, said he had no more details.
Zairean soldiers in the eastern Zairean lakeside town of Bukavu on Thursday stole two aid agency vehicles and beat up a Belgian World Food Programme staff member after they tried to steal his car.
Aid agency officials said they had been told the Zairean military was requisitioning their vehicles to evacuate their families from Bukavu, the target of advancing Banyamulenge rebels.
